name: Cassavel Lychee-Sumac Cola
description: A corporate attempt to capture the niche appeal of Halka Lychee-Sumac Spritz with a cola base — launched by Veldran as a flanker product to test the lychee-sour flavor segment. The result is competent but lacks soul.
flavor_profile: Standard cola sweetness undercut by artificial lychee musk and a tangy sumac sourness that fights the caramel notes rather than complementing them.
cultural_context: Widely seen as a cynical cash-grab by consumers familiar with the street brands Veldran was imitating. Holds a 'so bad it's funny' reputation in some Tier 2 circles and is occasionally ordered ironically at dive bars.
story_hooks: A Veldran flavor chemist leaked the Cassavel formula to a street brand before launch — Veldran's internal security is hunting them, and the chemist has gone quiet.
A shipment of Cassavel was found to contain elevated levels of a restricted mood-stabilizing compound — either contamination or something deliberate.
A Tier 2 community council is using Cassavel as a symbol in a larger campaign against corponation cultural appropriation of street-brand flavor identities.
